newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel says inflation now at lower rate.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel says inflation now at lower rate.

text.p: The Bank of Israel attributed its decision to lower interest rates to the fact that inflation is currently running at a slower pace than in the first half of the year.
In the first half of the year inflation was running at an annual rate of about 14.5 percent while in July the consumer price index rose by only 0.3 percent.
The central bank announced on Monday it would cut its key lending rate for September by 0.5 percentage point to an annual 15.8 percent.

In a statement, the central bank also said that a rise in interest rates in the first half had a positive impact on the capital market's inflationary expectations for the next 12 months, now at 10.6 percent against 13 percent in June.
Money supply as measured by M1 grew 4.5 percent in July but the central bank said the money supply expansion was in line with growth and should not create inflationary pressures.
On the other hand, inflation is still running at a rate that is beyond the government's 1996 target of 8-10 percent, the central bank warned.
Also, while recent data indicate a certain slowdown in economic growth, there is still surplus demand reflecting a rise in private and public consumption, it added.
This economic picture requires tight fiscal policy and continued tight monetary policy.

The central bank called on the government to correct as much as possible the deviation in this year's budget deficit target. The deficit is estimated to surpass by more than four billion shekels the target of 7.6 billion, the central bank said.
It also called for setting multi-year inflation targets that gradually decline to reach levels prevailing in Israel's main trading partners.
